findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator cannot handle datetime ordering used by audit logs
findings.body: get_item_key() calls math.floor() or math.ceil() on the value of self.key. When OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint uses OptimizedCursorPaginator with order_by="-datetime", this value is a datetime, so math.floor(datetime) raises TypeError: must be real number, not datetime. Any non-empty audit-log page requested with optimized_pagination=true by an allowed user will return a 500 instead of results. Additionally, value_from_cursor() returns cursor.value directly rather than converting it to a datetime like DateTimePaginator does, so cursor comparisons are not correct for datetime keys.

findings.title: Negative offset pagination slices a Django QuerySet with a negative start
findings.body: When enable_advanced_features is true and cursor.offset < 0, start_offset is set to the negative cursor offset and the code executes queryset[start_offset:stop]. Django QuerySet slicing does not support negative indexes and raises ValueError ("Negative indexing is not supported."), so the advertised negative-offset reverse pagination cannot work. A request such as cursor=0:-1:0&optimized_pagination=true from an authorized user will produce a server error instead of a page or a clean 400.

findings.title: No tests cover the new OptimizedCursorPaginator or the endpoint opt-in path
findings.body: The PR adds a new paginator with custom slicing and offset behavior and a new endpoint feature flag but does not change any tests. This leaves both the datetime ordering failure and the negative slice failure uncovered, so CI would not catch a broken optimized-pagination flow.
